plants.sentence: Because they split by thresholds, classification trees change when an ordered variable is given a monotone transformation, and they are sensitive to outliers and mislabelled training points.
A random forest lowers variance by combining diverse trees at no cost in bias, so it always gives a better model than any single tree.
Shrinkage works like a learning rate: it controls how fast the boosted model learns. Values closer to 1 reduce overfitting more than values closer to 0.

Each tree typically trains on about 67% of the examples and never sees the other 33%. Out-of-bag evaluation scores each example using only the trees that did not see it, which makes it exactly as accurate as 10-fold cross-validation.
Permutation importance shuffles one feature's values and measures how much the model's score drops; a large drop shows that changing that feature in the real world causes the target to change.
